text:
Sam: Heads-up — after the latest proxy tweak (half-close grace lowered) we got reports of ~40k WS clients in EU showing stalled UI for ~1s then resume.
Lina: saw that in the alert runbook thread. any repro?
Sam: yes, repro with our chrome test harness: client sends close, proxy responds 1000 but doesn't send FIN downstream for ~800ms, client reconnects and sits in ESTABLISHED but app-level handshake stalls.
Ravi: that sounds like TCP linger vs app-level close mismatch. Did we change tcp_fin_delay or just the half-close heuristic?
Sam: changed the half-close grace from 1.5s -> 0.2s to speed up route reclamation. The unexpected effect: backend kept streaming alive for a bit (drain bug), so the client ended up waiting on a chunk boundary.
Lina: console metrics show a spike in "sse/ws stall count" and a correlated increase in latency P95 for route-switch events.
Ravi: screenshots?
Sam: pasted small log: ```
[proxy] 2026-03-23T11:03:19Z conn=44abcd half_close=0.2s forwarded-close id=cli-77 route=eu-west
[backend] 2026-03-23T11:03:19.150 send-chunk id=cli-77 seq=124
[client] 2026-03-23T11:03:19.180 reconnect id=cli-77 new-route=eu-west-2
[proxy] 2026-03-23T11:03:19.950 handshake start id=cli-77
```
Lina: so new handshake starts while backend was finishing a chunk => client blocks on reading until the proxy finalizes FIN, weirdly counting as stall in our idle-detect metric.
Ravi: billing/console sees this as two sessions with small overlap in "active connections" metric?
Sam: yes, overlaps are <1s but they make the console show duplicate active rows and confuse support.
Lina: quick mitigation options: 1) revert half-close grace bump, 2) make proxy wait for backend chunk flush before claiming route, 3) tweak console to hide overlaps <1s. Thoughts?
Ravi: (3) is just masking the symptom; (2) is safer but requires careful backpressure handling. Revert (1) while we test (2).
Sam: agree. I'll open revert PR for canary and simultaneously a patch to proxy drain logic to prefer flushing in-flight chunks for up to 500ms before route claim.
Lina: telemetry ask: add a metric "route_claim_vs_last_chunk_delta" and a dashboard panel showing top routes and client ids, plus an alert if >0.2% of claims have delta < 1s.
Sam: also add sampling of raw client headers for stalled cases — we need UA/IP to correlate SDK versions that may be more sensitive.
Ravi: for rollout UX: console should annotate these short overlaps as "likely route swap, see trace" and link to the trace timeline. That reduces support noise.
OpsBot: canary rollback started by Lina at 11:12 UTC.
Lina: filing follow-ups: INFRA-2102 revert half-close on canary, INFRA-2103 proxy drain flush patch, METRICS-880 dashboard+alert.
Sam: i'll run stress harness with both SSE and WS flows to validate. Ravi — can you sanity-check the billing side for double-charge windows?
Ravi: yes, billing team should be robust but i'll run a quick sim. If billing charges on route claim, we need to add dedupe window or require first bytes. I'll post results.
Lina: thanks. keep ops/sdks in loop — maybe add client-side quick FIN on close to avoid lingering chunk windows.
Sam: copying sdks@, infra-billing@ in the RFC. :thumbsup:
Ravi: quick note — let's also ensure multipart chunking doesn't hold the socket open longer than necessary; might be a payload encoder quirk.
Lina: good catch. Everyone, sync meeting in 30 to review traces.
Sam: thanks all.
